triage.modern_statement: This can't be turned into a precise mathematical question. The transcription is garbled (several words are marked [?]), and the sentence is item 2 in a list comparing the geometric/axiomatic approach with the analytic or genetic approach to the real numbers. The most it supports is a methodological remark: that one approach might perhaps fill a 'gap' (Lücke) and solve problems the newer theory has left. There is no definite statement to check.
triage.answered_by: Not identifiable. The general theme of the page, genetic versus axiomatic foundations of the real numbers, later appears in Hilbert's 'Über den Zahlbegriff' (1900). It is also linked to the consistency of arithmetic, which is Problem 2 of his 1900 Paris list. But nothing ties this particular fragment to either.

evidence.claim: Hilbert set out an axiom system for the real numbers in 1900 ('Über den Zahlbegriff'), using the axiomatic approach as opposed to the genetic one. He also suggested a direct consistency proof for the arithmetical axioms 'by means of a careful study and suitable modification of the known methods of reasoning in the theory of irrational numbers' (Paris lecture, Problem 2).

triage.why: Even in translation the sentence makes no sense ('at which this mathematics has new teaching whole for it'), and it states no theorem or conjecture. It is best read as a methodological comment in a pros-and-cons comparison. The surrounding topic does lead into Hilbert's published work on the real-number axioms and the consistency of arithmetic (Problem 2). That problem is known and was historically shaped by Gödel and Gentzen, but matching this fragment to it would be speculation.
